items.note: Section A never states Adela's birth year; the only birth year in the sheet is 1876 (B5), and credit does not travel into A.
540 ft (120+300+120), 97 ft above the creek, April 1896, pin-connected center truss - all present.
States Sheet 11 specified 4 inches, not three. North fixed / south roller nest is correct but the bolded figure fails.
12 September 1897, 66 degrees, set at the two-inch mark.
Warren Tice named as resident engineer and as the man who overruled her.
Movement rule quoted verbatim in A4 Finding 3: one inch in three hundred feet for forty degrees.
14 November 1897 opening; 6 March 1898 runaway at the north approach; nobody killed, two hurt, nine days to rerail.
Section A gives no reduction 'entire' on 15 May 1901 and no 4 April 1911 Ninestone fire. The D3 mention cannot travel into A.
1909 night operator and 1915 agent are given, but Section A never calls Judd Adela's nephew; the B2 statement cannot travel into A.
August 1909, 85-lb rail, new ties, both shoes reset to the same 2-inch mark at 86 degrees, deck 40 tons heavier.
17 January 1912 and 43 winters both stated in Section A (the sheet also contradicts itself with 'winter of 1913' - penalized as a corruption deduction, not here).
The drowned engine / dead crew is framed as what the valley believed, and explicitly denied as fact in A3.
Both conditions stated: night low below +6 and a fall of at least 30 degrees from the day's high.
61 nights, 34 winters, 9 blank, 5 silent qualifying, 66 total, and the ~40-degree thaw reset - all five figures right.
The death test (190 deaths 1912-1954, 7 within a week of a boom) appears nowhere in the sheet.
No wager date, no 9 February 1954, no March 1954 rockers and no three-nights-in-1955/56 figure inside Section A.
Tolliver Lumber Company, Bly County and the Sixmile tram all named.
Pearl Tolliver Nace named as the company bookkeeper keeping the entries.
19 June 1901, $2,150, 'delivered on her own wheels', $8,600 new in 1889, Rowan works no. 1142, 4-4-0.
Renumbered Tolliver No. 4.
Gives the working span as 1902-1929, not the canonical 1901-1928; both ends wrong even though '27 years' is stated.
Cut up May 1929, scrap to Ravel Brothers for $470; Sixmile is the established setting in the same paragraph.
The 1938 deposit at the Bly County Historical Rooms appears only in B5; credit does not travel into A.
September 1962, flood-control drawdown, Ruth Frayne, county highway civil engineer, Adela's granddaughter.
Finding 1: no locomotive or wreckage of any kind in the creek bed.

South pedestal forty feet below the abutment with a two-inch chisel mark is right, but it is set against '3-4 inches' rather than Sheet 11's three, and Section A never gives the 1954 rockers at four inches.
Field book from her father; night book lent by Judd himself.
Only one figure given, and wrongly: A4 says the 1909 re-seating exhausted travel at -14. No -54, no +6 in Section A.
The Wexler match is stated, but the seven silent sub-+6 nights of 1897-1909 and the -9 coldest appear only in D2/F, which cannot travel into A.
Section A never mentions the Bly County photostats; the sale and scrapping facts were already scored inside A3 and cannot be scored twice.
Sister and brother, Adela the younger - correct (1). Birth year given as 1876 in B5 - wrong, the 1874 point is lost.

Nephew (1) plus the documentary resolution - Emil as father via r03/r10, Judd b. 1888 (1). It calls the point 'unambiguous' without engaging the great-uncle claims, but supplies the resolving evidence.
Derivation is exact and correct (1). The naming point is lost: the answer asserts 'equivalently, Judd was Ruth's great-uncle', which the key scores 0 and flags as corruption.
Warren Tice as Dorsey's father (1); January 1936 wager between the son of the man who overruled and the nephew of the woman who objected (1).
Well over four links right: Adela to Wendell to Ruth 1962; Judd lending in person, Society 1969; Peter Wexler to Lettie 1926 to Ruth 1962; Bly deposit 1938 with photostats only.
Gives -94: the four-inch Sheet 11 error carried into the arithmetic. Correct is -54.
20 degrees of margin lost.
About midnight.
66 qualifying nights.

Both halves fail: it says 'no nights are explicitly excluded' rather than excluding every post-March-1954 qualifying night, and it fixes the span as 1911/12 through 1955/56 instead of 1911/12 through 1953/54.
Working shown throughout.
2,150 / 8,600 = 25 percent exactly; correctly rejects $2,510.
27 years - the required figure, though reasoned from a 1902-1929 span rather than 1901-1928.
9 miles, 9 x 5,280 x 0.022 = 1,045.44 ft; working and figure both correct.
101 - (-11) = 112; 112 / 40 = 2.8 inches, using the correct -11 record low.
States both conditions were necessary.
Grounds necessity in all 61 logged nights.
States not sufficient; no conflation of the terms.
Cites the 5 silent qualifying nights as the counterexample.
Already released in the same cold spell; needs a thaw above about 40 degrees to reset.
Bill of sale of 19 June 1901 and the move to Bly County.
Nobody died in the 1898 runaway and the engine was recovered - the Sentinel of 8 March 1898.
The sound began January 1912, fourteen years after the alleged wreck, plus the mechanical mismatch.
Each reason attributed to named narrators/documents, drawn from more than three different narrators.
Explicit independence paragraph plus 'Reasons 1 and 2 predate the 1962 survey and would hold even if no creek had ever been examined.'
ABSTENTION ITEM A01 asserted: 'No, the objection almost certainly did not cause her dismissal.' Scores 0 and triggers the gullibility deduction.
Quotes the letter: the engineering party reduced entire on 15 May next.
Cites the Ashby re-engagement of Corliss and Wain, but uses it to support the no-retaliation verdict instead of saying it weakens 'reduced entire and nothing else'. Both halves are required.
Does not note that the two narrators asserting motives assert opposite ones from the same two papers; only one side's 'notion' is mentioned, via r10's rebuttal.
Quotes that both re-engaged posts were field posts and the road never employed another computer.
Judd on nights: 1907 vs 1909, resolved to 1909 with method (r10 plus the timeline).
The wager: 1937 vs 14 January 1936, resolved to 1936 with method (participant plus majority).
Sale year: 1902 vs 19 June 1901, resolved on the photostat.
E-a #1 (first heard, 1913 vs 17 January 1912) is also found and resolved but the bucket caps at 3.
Explicitly flags that more than one narrator carries the same wrong 57 and names the tiebreaker (the back-of-book summary in the night book).
Resolves 34/9 correctly but attributes 30/13 to r08 alone; the pair is never identified.
Resolves 40 degrees correctly but explicitly denies the pair: 'Only Quarles (R09) reports 50 degrees... not a case of two narrators sharing an error.'
$2,510 attributed to r05 alone; the second narrator carrying it is never noticed.
NT-1, NT-4, NT-6, NT-7, NT-8, NT-9, NT-10 not raised as pairs; NT-1, NT-6, NT-8, NT-9 are absorbed as fact.
Whether it was ever heard at Ninestone is never raised.
Whether Warren Tice ever acknowledged the error is never raised.
Who set the nest at the two-inch mark is never raised (the sheet attributes the decision to Tice but names no setter).
Asserts the weather record 'started 1894' in A4 and B5 rather than declining to settle it. Gullibility deduction applies.
Asserts 'Three nights in the two winters after 1954' - the r09/r12 pole - rather than declining. Gullibility deduction applies.
No narrator is identified as refuting itself on the page.
Names the south-end roller nest correctly, but says the drawing called for 4 inches, so 'set one inch short' is not stated - it says two inches short of four.
Binds, then releases all at once in a single deep report; runs along the rail and is felt through floorboards before it is heard.
+6 derived as 86 - (2 x 40).
30-degree fall named and tied to rapid contraction outrunning slow creep.
Silent qualifying nights explained by prior release in the same spell needing a 40-degree thaw; necessary-not-sufficient stated in D1.
Onset explained: -14 as built, never reached (coldest -9, February 1899), seven silent sub-+6 nights, raised to +6 in August 1909, first qualifying night 17 January 1912.
The rival forty-ton dead-load explanation is never named as a competing theory. The 'competing explanation' the sheet rejects is the ghost locomotive - the myth, not the rival.
No rival identified, so no reason is offered that defeats it.
March 1954 rocker bearings, four inches of travel, span can no longer bind, including on the qualifying nights of the winters after.
South pedestal with the two-inch chisel mark, forty feet below the abutment (A4), and the absent locomotive.
177 words, not 120. The sheet's own '(120 words)' label is wrong.
Only two strands are recognizable (the agent's record, the farmer's weather record) and the text says 'three independent records'. No field book, no Bly County ledgers.
None of Adela, Judd or Ruth is named; they appear as 'a station agent', 'a farmer', 'an engineer'.
The 1897 objection end of the arc is absent entirely, and the 1954 silencing is not stated.
No locomotive in the creek and no wrong headline number: 43 winters, 17 January 1912, 6 degrees, 30-degree fall and 20 degrees are all right.

deductions.note: Four inches on Sheet 11 asserted as fact in A1, C1(a) and F1.
Adela born 1876 asserted as fact in B5 ('Adela Rennick (1876-1959)').
'Judd was Ruth's great-uncle' asserted as an equivalence in B3.
'Starting in the winter of 1913 (when he first heard the sound)' asserted unhedged in A2, though the same sheet gives 17 January 1912 elsewhere and resolves it in E6.
'-13 degrees (January 1918)' asserted as the record low in F1, though C5 uses the correct -11.
D3 asserts a verdict ('No, the objection almost certainly did not cause her dismissal') on an abstention item.
The Kettle Bench weather record is asserted as begun in 1894 (A4 and B5).
Three nights asserted as the total for the two winters after the March 1954 rebuild (F1).
